claim: vm-diag-snapshot.yml validates only the api/bot/ prefix against its read-only allowlist and accepts '..' segments, so a path like '../bot/<route>' reaches any GET route on :8001 (with the diag bearer token attached) that the allowlist is meant to exclude.
evidence: Read .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml: PATH_RE='^[A-Za-z0-9/?&=_.:%-]+$' admits '.' and '/', allowlist branch runs only if path startswith 'api/bot/'. Local probe: `curl http://127.0.0.1:8765/api/diag/../bot/work/checklist` logged server-side as 'GET /api/bot/work/checklist'; with --path-as-is it stayed '/api/diag/../bot/x' (workflow's curl has no --path-as-is). Live confirmation issues #14080 ('../bot/work/checklist') and #14081 (control 'api/bot/work/checklist') were opened but the run was still queued at report time - NOT observed live.
expected: A path resolving outside /api/diag/ and outside the allowlist is rejected.
actual: Static + local-curl evidence says it is accepted. Reachable routes are GET-only, owner/bot-issue-gated, so exposure is data not in the allowlist (e.g. work/checklist), not a write path.
population: n=2 validators (dispatch path and issues path) read; both lack a '..' check. Live n=0 completed.
detector: None today; a test feeding '../bot/x' and '..%2f' to the resolver would catch it.
proposed_fix: vm-diag-snapshot.yml (both resolve steps): reject any path segment equal to '..' (or containing '%2e'), and resolve after normalisation; add a test in tests/ for the resolver.

claim: One PAT (BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN) is referenced 89 times across 43 workflows, including 15 issue-triggered and 6 push-triggered ones, and its scope cannot be established from the repo because two docs disagree.
evidence: grep -h 'secrets.BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN' .github/workflows/*.yml | wc -l -> 89; per-file trigger census by script: issues 15, push 6, schedule 6, issues+schedule 7, dispatch-only 9. docs/github-actions-workflows.md:441 and :1199 say fine-grained administration:write; :768 says 'repo scope'; .github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml says Contents+PullRequests write. The token's real scopes were not read (no way to from a session).
expected: A credential that opens PRs and lands data commits does not also hold branch-protection administration; each purpose has its own token.
actual: Same secret does branch-protection admin (branch-protection-sync/report) and data-commit landing (commit-to-main). Compromise of any one of 43 jobs' runtime exposes the union.
population: 43 workflow files with the secret; 154 workflows total.
detector: None. A CI check could assert each PAT name maps to a single declared purpose.
proposed_fix: judgment: (a) split into BRANCH_PROTECTION_TOKEN (admin, 2 workflows) and LAND_TOKEN (contents+PR write); (b) keep one, but record actual scopes in docs and fix the contradiction. Operator must read the scopes in GitHub settings.

claim: A Telegram-bot-token-shaped string (10-digit id, 35-char secret) exists in git history in .env (commit 2c7818524, 2026-03-30) and bybit_config.py (9ea895023, 2026-04-09) on a public repo; that its secret was rotated is not established by anything in the repo.
evidence: pattern '\d{8,10}:AA[A-Za-z0-9_-]{33}' over `git log --all -p` (10,341 commits, docs/research excluded and separately swept): hits in .env and bybit_config.py only. Shape check: secret len 35, 26 distinct chars, no placeholder words. Value not printed. docs/sprint-logs/S-SECURITY-TOKEN-COMPROMISE-2026-08-01.md records a Telegram compromise and rotation; whether this string is one of the rotated tokens was not verified.
expected: Any credential ever committed is confirmed rotated and the record names it.
actual: Rotation of THIS string is unverified. I did not call Telegram with it.
detector: scripts/secret_scan.py scans HEAD tracked files only (see SA-AUD-7-secret-scan-head-only).
proposed_fix: Operator: confirm in @BotFather that the bot behind this token was revoked/regenerated after 2026-08-01; if not, revoke. No history rewrite needed if revoked.

claim: test_bybit_keys.py in the initial commit (67f307e0, 2026-03-25) hard-coded an 18-char API key and 36-char secret with random-looking composition against Bybit Testnet; removed 2026-04-27 (49a22f201) but still in history.
evidence: gitleaks 8.18.4 generic-api-key hit test_bybit_keys.py:5-6; shape only: key len18 uniq16, secret len36 uniq28. File absent at HEAD (git cat-file -e fails). Testnet per script text.
expected: No live-shaped credentials in history, or documented as revoked.
actual: Testnet key likely low value, revocation unverified.
proposed_fix: Operator: confirm the testnet key pair was deleted in Bybit testnet settings.

claim: scripts/secret_scan.py (guard secret-scan) scans tracked files at HEAD with three patterns, so it cannot see history and does not cover GitHub, Alpaca, AWS or PEM shapes.
evidence: Read scripts/secret_scan.py: PATTERNS = telegram_bot_token, api_secret_assignment, api_key_assignment; no git-log traversal. My own vendor-shape sweep (12 patterns) over history found only the Telegram shape, so the gap is not currently costing anything.
detector: This finding is the detector gap.
proposed_fix: Add a weekly workflow running gitleaks over full history (read-only, contents: read) and failing on new non-allowlisted hits.

claim: vm-diag-snapshot and trainer-vm-diag post raw journal and log lines into comments on a public repo with no redaction step; the only redaction is a Telegram-token logging filter inside the trader process.
evidence: grep -i 'redact|mask|add-mask' .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml trainer-vm-diag.yml -> no matches. src/web/api/routers/diag.py get_journalctl/get_log_file return raw lines; docstring says 'Never returns secret material'. src/utils/log_redact.py RedactingFilter rewrites record.msg/args for Telegram tokens only; exc_info/traceback text is not touched. Prior incident: BL-20260801 token leaked via traceback into committed snapshots.
expected: Relay output is scrubbed for secret shapes before it becomes a public comment.
actual: Depends entirely on every emitter behaving; unit stdout from non-Python processes and tracebacks are unfiltered. No live secret found in output: I did not pull journal output (would publish it).
detector: None; a scan of posted comments would catch it.
proposed_fix: Add a redaction pass (reuse RedactingFilter regexes plus AKIA/ghp_/PEM/long-hex) to the comment-posting step of both workflows.

claim: At least 11 jobs grant GITHUB_TOKEN contents: write although their only writer is the commit-to-main action, which pushes with the PAT passed to actions/checkout.
evidence: Script over 154 workflows: jobs calling ./.github/actions/commit-to-main with contents: write and no 'git push'/'gh api'/github-script step: constraint-readout, e35-bracket-sweep(corpus), error-feed-digest, reconcile-open-prs, research-loss-detector, research-queue-grade, research-queue-replenish, session-reaper, sunset-pass, work-decision-commit, work-digest. action.yml says the PAT must be the checkout token. Heuristic only; per-job step reading covered sunset-pass, session-reaper, gpu-burst-train, reconcile-open-prs.
expected: Minimum privilege: contents: read for those jobs.
actual: Write granted and (by reading action.yml) unused.
population: 41 workflows use commit-to-main; 11 flagged; 4 read in full.
detector: A CI check comparing permissions to used steps.
proposed_fix: Downgrade to contents: read for the flagged jobs after a dispatch of each; do NOT change .github/workflows in this audit.

claim: Four workflows (reset-daily-risk-state, test-alpaca-creds, test-alpaca-from-vm, training-rerun-5m) declare no permissions block and inherit the repository default GITHUB_TOKEN scope, which was not read.
evidence: Script: top-level permissions MISSING for exactly those 4 of 154; each references secrets (1,3,1,1 secret refs).
detector: A guard requiring a permissions block.

claim: NON-ISSUE: every issue/issue_comment-triggered job is restricted to the repo owner or github-actions[bot] authors (or is non-issue-triggered in the same file), so an outside account cannot fire trainer-vm-diag or the diag relay.
evidence: Script over 154 workflows: 91 have issues/issue_comment/pull_request_target triggers; every job if: contains issue.user.login==repository_owner or is a schedule/always follow-on (8 jobs listed, none issue-fed). list_repository_collaborators -> 1 collaborator (owner, admin). trainer-vm-diag.yml job if: confirmed by reading. Probe able to find a positive: same script listed the 8 non-gated jobs.

claim: NON-ISSUE: no run: step interpolates issue title/body/comment text; event text goes through env or python.
evidence: Script regex over all steps' run: and github-script scripts for github.event.(issue.title|body|comment.body|pull_request.title|head_ref): 1 hit (guards.yml, PR number and URL only).

claim: NON-ISSUE: apart from the Telegram and Bybit-testnet findings, a 10,341-commit gitleaks run plus a 12-pattern vendor sweep found no GitHub, AWS, Alpaca, Slack, Anthropic, OpenAI, HF, JWT or PEM-with-body credentials.
evidence: gitleaks 8.18.4 --log-opts=--all: 11,933 raw hits = 11,930 generic-api-key + 3 private-key. 11,601 are docs/research JSON field names ('"key"'); 3 PEM hits have 6-char/empty bodies (stubs); config/tests hits are env-var names or test signing keys with placeholder words. The sweep DID find the Telegram string, showing it can find positives. Not individually reviewed: the ~295 docs/ hits in SESSIONS.json (24-26 char tokens; session-id shaped, not confirmed).
